term: "Test Set"

difficulty: "Beginner"

## Simple explanation

A test set is a group of examples kept separate from model training and
tuning. It provides a final check of how well the chosen model may perform
on new data.

## Technical explanation

The test set is held out from parameter fitting and model selection, then
used to estimate generalization under an evaluation design. Repeatedly
using test results to make choices leaks information from the test set into
development and makes the reported estimate optimistic.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

A well-managed test set helps teams compare the final system with
baselines and communicate expected performance. Its representativeness,
label quality, and independence from training data are as important as its
size.

## How it works

Partition data into training, validation, and test subsets using splits
appropriate to the use case, such as time-based or group-based splits.
Tune decisions on training and validation data, lock the approach, and
evaluate on the test set once for the final estimate.

## Practical example

For a model that predicts future equipment failures, a chronological test
set can contain the most recent period. This checks temporal generalization
more realistically than a random split if deployment predicts future
events.

## Common misconceptions

- A large test set can still give a misleading estimate if it differs from
  deployment data.
- The test set should not be used repeatedly for hyperparameter tuning or
  threshold selection.
